long_biography.plain_text:
Wace spent eleven years at S.G. Warburg, becoming a director and leading European equity sales, proprietary trading and international trading. He then headed equity and derivatives trading at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell before co-founding Marshall Wace with Paul Marshall in 1997. As chief executive, Wace oversaw the firm's growth and development across its international operations.

Marshall Wace built its business around long-short equity and other liquid alternative strategies, including its proprietary TOPS system. KKR later acquired a strategic minority interest that now represents roughly two-fifths of the group, while Wace remains a member and founding partner. His fortune is best understood as founder equity and income from the management company. Capital managed for clients, securities held by funds and the value of Marshall Wace as a business are separate from his personal assets.
